definition: A work period assigned without pay, benefits, or Diaspora-logged hours — typically enforced on undocumented workers or those under coercive contracts. The hours exist in corporate records but generate no traceable compensation trail. Common practice in Ringo Heavy Industries' subcontracting chains.
origin: Corporate jargon turned street slang; originally an internal Ringo scheduling term that leaked into worker communities
usage: Used by labor organizers, Tier 1-2 workers, and investigative journalists covering wage theft
example: Twenty hours of null shift every week — legal on paper because the contract defines them as 'orientation continuation periods.'
